overview: Kilwa Kisiwani was a Swahili coastal center connected to Indian Ocean exchange. Surviving mosques, palace buildings and houses reveal a city shaped by commerce, Islamic practice and local construction knowledge.

items.text: Builders used coral stone and lime mortar. The Great Mosque incorporated domes and vaults rather than a simple flat roof.
Embedded Chinese porcelain decorated parts of the mosque, incorporating imported objects into local architecture.
The Husuni Kubwa palace included an octagonal bathing pool; houses, squares and burial grounds formed a broader urban landscape.
Kilwa and neighboring Songo Mnara provide evidence for extensive maritime trade and the growth of Swahili coastal culture.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara
